question: What do I check before starting a new fire pump drive engine for the first time?
reference_answer: Before starting, make sure the cooling and lubrication systems are filled to the proper levels. Complete the safety checks, remove tools and foreign objects, secure all guards and alert people nearby. Then check: (1) no apparent damage and all components fitted; (2) drive belt properly installed; (3) hoses and tubes properly installed; (4) electrical connections properly installed; (5) installation follows the pump manufacturer's instructions, with correct alignment and free rotation; (6) lubricate the auxiliary drive shaft grease fittings. question: How do I do the weekly battery maintenance?
reference_answer: Ventilate the battery compartment before servicing. Wear protective clothing, impervious neoprene gloves and goggles or a full-face shield. (1) Wipe dirt off with a damp cloth. (2) Check each cell with a hydrometer. Fully charged is 1.260; this weekly-maintenance section says replace the battery below 1.215. (3) Check wiring, both alternator connectors, battery connections and the engine grounding lug. For corrosion, remove the negative cable first, clean clamps and cables with emery cloth or a wire brush, then wash terminals with 2 oz (1/4 cup) baking soda in 0.94 L (1 qt) water. Keep this solution out of the cells. Flush with clean water, apply a light coat of petroleum jelly, and refit and tighten the clamps. (4) Check electrolyte monthly and top up with distilled water to the bottom of the filler neck. (5) Check continuity and insulation resistance to ground, and correct electrical faults. (6) Refit the cables, negative last.

question: How is the drive shaft lubricated?
reference_answer: (1) Remove the drive shaft guards. (2) Wipe the grease fittings and the grease gun nozzle with a clean cloth. (3) Add grease to the universal joint grease fittings. (4) Wipe excess grease from the fittings.

question: How do I remove and reinstall the coolant thermostat?
reference_answer: Follow the engine manual for the complete instructions. Use the correct thermostat and never operate without one. (1) Remove the upper coolant hose clamps and hose at the thermostat housing. (2) Remove the two flange cap screws and flange. (3) Remove the thermostat and gasket. (4) Clean dirt, oxidation and sludge off the housing flange faces. (5) Refit the thermostat if it is still in good condition. Inspect the flange seal and replace it if damaged or cracked. (6) Refit the flange and cap screws.

question: How do I start and stop the engine locally at the digital panel?
reference_answer: Complete the safety checks, remove tools and foreign objects, secure all guards and alert people nearby. To start locally, press AUTO/MAN to select MANUAL, then press CRANK BATT A and/or CRANK BATT B. To stop, press RESET/STOP or hold the red Engine STOP button on the left of the panel until the engine stops. If pump-on-demand is still present, releasing Engine STOP makes the engine try to restart. Stop it at the fire pump controller as well.

question: The speed of my electronic fixed-speed engine does not match the factory setting plate. How do I adjust it?
reference_answer: For electronic fixed-speed engines only. (1) From the main screen, select ECM A. (2) Press MENU. (3) Press RPM ADJUSTMENT. (4) Use INC or DEC, 10 RPM per press, within +/-50 RPM. (5) Press RETURN. (6) Press RESET/STOP and wait 30 seconds. (7) Repeat steps 1-5 for ECM B. Never switch from ECM A to ECM B while the engine is running.

reference_answer: Only no. 2 diesel fuel (ASTM no. 2D). Other fuel may affect emissions, and adjustments to make up for an alternative fuel are not warrantable.

question: At the first start the gauge shows no oil pressure, or the low oil pressure message appears within fifteen seconds. What do I do?
reference_answer: Stop the engine immediately. Continued operation without proper lubrication damages the engine.

question: The engine did not start automatically in a fire emergency. How do I start it by hand?
reference_answer: (1) Open the water bypass valves in the cooling water supply, or the emergency cooling supply. (2) Press the AUTO/MAN switch to put the engine in manual mode. (3) Open the panel door, slide the key switch override to the right and check that LED 49 KEY FB is lit. Do not crank for more than fifteen seconds, wait fifteen seconds between attempts, up to six attempts. (4) Press down on the Battery A or the Battery B contactor lever. If A does not engage the starter, use B; if the batteries are weak, press both together. Release the lever as soon as the engine starts. If it has not started after three attempts, check the fuel supply: no blue or white exhaust smoke while cranking means no fuel is delivered. (5) Check that the engine runs at rated speed and shows oil pressure within fifteen seconds.

question: How do I do the weekly test run and what do I check during it?
reference_answer: Start the engine at least weekly and run it for at least 30 minutes with as much load as possible. Keep no-load operation to a minimum. Check: (1) oil pressure appears within 15 seconds; (2) normal running temperature after at least 30 minutes; (3) proper operating speed, referring to the engine operation checks if incorrect; (4) no unusual noise; (5) oil pressure above 69 kPa (10 psi); (6) coolant between 70 and 107 C (158-225 F); (7) both voltmeters show 12 VDC for standard or 24 VDC for optional systems; (8) the air-filter service indicator has not popped up. Replace the air filter as required if it indicates blockage. End the run by holding RESET/STOP until the engine stops.

question: How do I change the engine oil and filter?
reference_answer: Change the oil at least annually. Avoid contact with hot or used oil and dispose of it under local environmental rules. For composite oil pans, use a new drain-plug sealing washer and hold the external locking nut while tightening. (1) Run until coolant reaches 70 C (158 F), then shut off. (2) Place a suitable container under the drain plug. (3) Remove the plug and drain immediately. (4) Clean around the filter and remove it with a filter wrench. Discard any O-ring left on the flange, clean the flange with a lint-free cloth, and oil the new gasket with 15W-40. (5) Fill the new filter with high-quality 15W-40. (6) Center the filter on the threaded nipple and screw on until the gasket is snug, then add 1/4 turn. Do not overtighten. (7) Clean the drain-plug threads and sealing surface, refit the plug and torque as specified. (8) Fill the engine to the proper level with clean 15W-40. (9) Restart for 1-2 minutes; shut down if no oil pressure appears within 15 seconds. (10) Stop. (11) Wait about 15 minutes. (12) Check again and top up to H.

question: How is the heat exchanger pressure tested when an internal leak is suspected, and what if it leaks?
reference_answer: (1) Fit an adapter at the heat exchanger cooling-water outlet. Use pipe sealant to prevent setup leaks and use the fitting sizes on the engine data sheet. (2) Fit the test setup with a 689 kPa (100 psi) gauge at the cooling-water inlet. (3) Apply air at 276 kPa (40 psi), isolate the source and watch the gauge for 5 minutes. Pressure must remain unchanged. (4) Release the pressure before removing the tubing adapters, plug and test equipment. (5) Replace the heat exchanger if leakage is detected.

question: How do I change the fuel filters, and what if the engine does not restart?
reference_answer: Keep sparks and open flames away and clean spilled fuel immediately. (1) Shut off the engine. (2) Close fuel valves if fitted. (3) Clean around the filter or separator heads. (4) Remove the old canisters with a filter wrench. (5) Clean sludge and foreign particles off the heads and gasket surfaces. (6) Oil the gasket seals with clean SAE 15W-40. (7) Center each filter on the threaded nipple, screw on until snug, then add 1/4 turn. Do not overtighten. (8) Open the fuel valves. (9) Press CRANK BATT A or B. (10) Hold the contactor switch for no more than 15 seconds or until the engine starts. Wait 15 seconds between attempts. If it has not started after three attempts, check the fuel supply system. No blue or white exhaust smoke while cranking indicates no fuel delivery.

question: How do I run the overspeed test from the panel, and what happens at the end?
reference_answer: (1) Press MENU. (2) Press OVERSPEED TEST. (3) If needed, press RPM ADJUSTMENT and use INC and DEC to change the speed in steps of ten RPM. (4) Press RUN. (5) A dialog warns that the engine will ramp to overspeed. If it is safe, select Yes; if not, select No. (6) When the timer expires, ENGINE OVERSPEED flashes in red at the top of the screen. (7) The engine goes to manual mode until reset. (8) Press the RESET/STOP switch to reset it.

question: I held the Engine STOP button until the engine stopped, let go, and the engine started again. Why?
reference_answer: When the button is released the engine tries to restart if the fire pump controller still sends a pump-on-demand signal. The engine must also be stopped at the fire pump controller.

question: The coolant gauge on the panel has gone yellow and the engine is cold, below 100 °F. Is something wrong?
reference_answer: Yellow below 100 °F (38 °C) comes with a low coolant temperature fault (low engine temperature, TB-312). The gauge is also yellow between 200 and 211 °F (93 and 100 °C).

question: What pressure are the cooling loop water pressure regulators set to on a CFP60E?
